2022 AUDI RS6 AVANT

EXECUTIVE PACKAGE, SPORT EXHAUST, CARBON OPTIC PACKAGE, AND MORE!

OVERVIEW
The 2022 Audi RS6 Avant is a family hauler that blends versatility, V8 grunt, and executive luxury into a single, dominant package. It's the first RS6 Avant to make it stateside since the introduction of the C5 RS6 Avant 20 years ago (2002-2004), making it a much-anticipated vehicle. Behind its aggressive front fascia lies a 4.0L twin-turbocharged V8, paired with a 48-volt mild-hybrid system, producing an immense 591 horsepower and 590 lb-ft of torque. Power is routed through an 8-speed automatic transmission to Quattro all-wheel drive, enabling 0-60 mph in just 3.5 seconds. With dynamic ride control suspension, carbon ceramic brakes, and torque vectoring, the RS6 Avant feels agile and composed, delivering the precision of a sports car with the stability of a grand tourer. Few vehicles can balance speed and comfort so effortlessly. Stylistically, this Audi grabs attention with its RS-Honeycomb grille, widened fenders, carbon fiber trim, and massive wheels. The wagon's extended roofline flows into a muscular rear end with oval RS exhaust outlets to bring the sporty look together. Inside, black Valcona leather sport seats, carbon fiber inlays, and Bang & Olufsen audio create a cabin that's as cutting-edge as it is indulgent. Ferocious yet refined, the Audi RS6 Avant delivers exceptional dynamics and daily drivability in a family-friendly package––proving that performance and practicality don't have to live in separate garages.

Safety and Security
  • Forward collision mitigation - Forward thinking. You look away for just a second and suddenly the vehicle in front of you has stopped. That's when the forward collision mitigation system comes to life. When it senses an impending impact, it will activate a combination of features to help prevent or reduce the severity of an accident. Forward collision mitigation is always looking ahead.
  • Pedestrian impact prevention - An extra step toward safety. Pedestrians don't always stop, look, and listen, but with Pedestrian Impact Prevention, your vehicle is equipped to better see them and avoid them. This system constantly monitors the road ahead to identify and track pedestrians. It projects that image to an interior display screen, AND should an impact become likely, Pedestrian impact prevention takes steps to avoid a collision.
  • Hands-on cruise control. Set it and forget it. Road trips used to be stressful. Cruise control only managed speed, but not distance or safety. Now, with hands-on cruise control, simply set your desired speed and let sensor technology maintain a safe distance between you and surrounding vehicles. It slows you down, speeds you up and even keeps you in your own lane. Meet your ultimate co-pilot with hands-on cruise control.
Technology and Telematics
  • Smart device mirroring - Smartphone, meet smart car. You can control your device through your vehicle's infotainment system. Smart device mirroring brings together safety and convenience by making it easier to find what you're looking for while keeping your eyes on the road.
  • Mobile hotspot - WiFi on the fly. Connect your devices to the Internet through your vehicle's private mobile hotspot and take the internet wherever your journey takes you, without eating up your data allowance. Find the hotspot with mobile hotspot.

Distance pacing cruise control, your ultimate co-pilot.
    Safety and Security
    • Forward collision mitigation - Forward thinking. You look away for just a second and suddenly the vehicle in front of you has stopped. That's when the forward collision mitigation system comes to life. When it senses an impending impact, it will activate a combination of features to help prevent or reduce the severity of an accident. Forward collision mitigation is always looking ahead.

Pedestrians don't always stop, look, and listen, but with Pedestrian Impact Prevention, your vehicle is equipped to better see them and avoid them. This system constantly monitors the road ahead to identify and track pedestrians. It projects that image to an interior display screen, AND should an impact become likely, Pedestrian impact prevention takes steps to avoid a collision.

2019 Nissan Frontier S Basic, Reliable Work Truck with Proven Mechanical Simplicity

This 2019 Nissan Frontier S is the entry-level trim of Nissans long-running midsize pickup, built around durability and low-cost utility rather than comfort or modern tech. Its powered by a 2.5L inline-4 engine paired with a 5-speed automatic transmission, driving the rear wheels in this configuration.

Performance & Drivetrain
2.5L DOHC inline-4 engine (152 hp/171 lb-ft torque)
5-speed automatic transmission with overdrive
Rear-Wheel Drive (RWD)
Simple mechanical layout designed for durability and low maintenance
Max towing capacity (4-cyl): ~3,500 lbs depending on configuration
Real-World Driving Character
Slow acceleration compared to V6 competitors
Best suited for light hauling, small trailers, and work duty
Stable at highway speeds but not refined or quiet
Steering and ride feel more truck-like than modern midsize pickups
Interior & Features (Base S Trim)
Basic cloth seating
Manual or minimal power accessories depending on package
Simple dashboard layout with small infotainment screen (updated in later 2019 trims)
Rearview camera standard
Bluetooth connectivity (basic integration)
Capability & Utility
Strong payload capability for its class (varies ~9001,400 lbs)
Compact footprint makes it easy to maneuver in tight job sites
Durable frame and suspension designed for long-term work use
Simple drivetrain = fewer electronics, fewer failure points
Known Strengths (what makes it sell)
Very reliable reputation for the 2.5L engine when maintained
Low purchase price compared to newer trucks
Easy and inexpensive to maintain
Good beater work truck or fleet-style utility vehicle
Known Weaknesses (important for sales honesty)
Underpowered for modern expectations (especially on highways)
Outdated interior and infotainment
Poor fuel economy compared to newer midsize trucks
Ride quality is stiff and basic
Limited safety/driver-assist technology

(Industry reviews consistently note it as outdated but durable)

Bottom line

The 2019 Frontier S 2.5L is best positioned as:

a budget work truck
a reliable second vehicle
or a fleet/utilitarian pickup

With 78,606 miles on the clock and Subaru's legendary symmetrical AWD under the hood, this is the kind of vehicle that earns its reputation every single day — on the freeway, in the mountains, and everywhere in between.
About This 2015 Subaru Outback 2.5i Premium At just over 78,000 miles, this 2015 Subaru Outback sits comfortably in the sweet spot of used car ownership — broken in enough to have proven itself, but with plenty of life left ahead. Subaru Outbacks regularly push past 200,000 miles with proper maintenance, which means this one could easily have another 120,000+ miles to give. Whether you're commuting daily from Colton to San Bernardino, heading up to Big Bear Lake on the weekends, or hauling gear for a family road trip, this Outback is built to handle it without complaint. Stock #DA4579 is on the lot now — come see it in person before it's gone.
2015 Subaru Outback Performance and Engine2.5-Liter PZEV Four-Cylinder Engine Under the hood sits Subaru's tried-and-true 2.5-liter horizontally-opposed four-cylinder engine, rated at 175 horsepower and 174 lb-ft of torque. The PZEV (Partial Zero Emissions Vehicle) designation means this engine is tuned to run cleaner than standard gasoline engines — a plus for California emissions compliance and for buyers who care about their environmental footprint.
CVT with Manual Mode and Symmetrical AWD Paired to the engine is a continuously variable transmission (CVT) with manual mode paddle shifters, giving you the smoothness of an automatic with the control of a manual when you want it. Subaru's symmetrical all-wheel drive system is always engaged — not a part-time system that kicks in only when it slips. That means consistent traction on rain-slicked Southern California freeways, sandy desert roads, and mountain passes alike. Ground clearance of 8.7 inches rounds out the package, letting you tackle light off-road terrain without flinching.
Subaru Outback Features and InteriorWhat the 2.5i Premium Trim Includes The Premium trim steps up meaningfully from the base model. You can expect features like a power moonroof/sunroof, heated front seats — a genuine luxury on cold Inland Empire mornings — and a leather-wrapped steering wheel. The infotainment system includes Bluetooth audio streaming and hands-free calling, along with a touchscreen interface and SiriusXM satellite radio capability. Alloy wheels, roof rails for cargo carriers or bike racks, and automatic climate control round out a package that punches well above its price point in the used market.

The rear cargo area is one of the Outback's biggest selling points — 35.5 cubic feet behind the rear seats and 73.3 cubic feet with them folded flat. Whether you're picking up furniture, loading camping gear, or making a Costco run from the Ontario Mills area, this wagon-meets-SUV layout earns its keep every week.
Subaru Outback Reliability and Ownership The 2015 Subaru Outback has a strong reputation among owners and automotive reviewers alike. J.D. Power gave the 2015 Outback high marks for dependability, and it's consistently ranked among the most reliable used vehicles in the midsize SUV/wagon segment. The 2.5-liter engine in this generation is notably robust — owners frequently report crossing 150,000 and 200,000 miles with nothing more than routine oil changes, tire rotations, and a timing belt service around 100,000 miles.

One thing prospective buyers should be aware of: Subaru's 2.5-liter engine from this era has been associated with oil consumption in some units, so it's always worth checking the oil level periodically and asking your mechanic to keep an eye on it at service intervals. That said, the vast majority of 2015 Outback owners report no significant issues, and this is one of the reasons the model holds its resale value so well throughout California and nationwide.
Why Buy From Diamond Auto Exchange in Colton, California Diamond Auto Exchange has built its reputation in the Inland Empire by offering quality pre-owned vehicles at honest prices. Located in Colton, the dealership is conveniently accessible from San Bernardino, Riverside, Fontana, Rialto, and Ontario — making it an easy stop whether you're coming from the west side of the valley or heading in from the high desert. The team at Diamond Auto Exchange understands that buying a used car should feel straightforward, not stressful. They work with buyers at every stage — first-time car owners, families upgrading, and experienced buyers who know exactly what they want. Give them a call at 909-533-4657 to ask about this Outback or schedule a time to come see it.
Financing a Used Subaru Outback Near Colton Worried about financing? Diamond Auto Exchange works with a range of lenders to help buyers throughout the Inland Empire get behind the wheel. Whether you have excellent credit, are rebuilding your credit history, or are somewhere in between, there are options available to make this 2015 Subaru Outback work within your monthly budget. Buyers from Redlands, Loma Linda, Grand Terrace, Bloomington, and surrounding communities are encouraged to apply — the process is simple and the team will walk you through every step. Call 909-533-4657 or stop by the lot to get the conversation started.
Frequently Asked QuestionsIs the 2015 Subaru Outback a good buy? Yes — the 2015 Subaru Outback is widely considered one of the best used vehicle purchases in its segment. It combines standard all-wheel drive, wagon-level cargo room, solid fuel economy, and a reputation for longevity that few competitors can match. At 78,606 miles, this example has plenty of useful life remaining.
How many miles is too many on a 2015 Subaru Outback? With proper maintenance, a 2015 Subaru Outback can comfortably reach 200,000 miles or more. At 78,606 miles, this vehicle is well within a healthy range and represents a strong value in the used car market. The key factors are service history and oil consumption — both worth discussing with the dealer.
What does the 2.5i Premium trim include on the 2015 Outback? The 2.5i Premium trim adds a power moonroof, heated front seats, a leather-wrapped steering wheel, alloy wheels, roof rails, and an upgraded infotainment system with Bluetooth and SiriusXM compared to the base 2.5i. It's a meaningful step up in comfort and convenience.
Does the 2015 Subaru Outback have all-wheel drive? Yes. All 2015 Subaru Outbacks come standard with Subaru's symmetrical all-wheel drive system. Unlike many competitors that offer AWD only as an option or use part-time systems, Subaru's AWD is full-time and always engaged — providing consistent traction in all driving conditions.
Is a CVT transmission reliable in the 2015 Subaru Outback? Subaru's Lineartronic CVT has proven to be reliable in the 2015 Outback generation. As with any transmission, keeping up with fluid changes at recommended intervals is the best way to protect it long-term. Most owners report smooth, trouble-free operation well past 100,000 miles.

description:
Ford brought the Ranger back in 2019 after a long absence from the American market, and it returned better than ever. This 2019 Ranger XLT SuperCrew in Lightning Blue Metallic is a perfect example of why mid-size truck buyers have been clamoring for exactly this kind of vehicle. Big enough to work, small enough to live with every day, and packed with more technology and capability than any Ranger that came before it. At $25,500 and 69,092 miles, this is a competitively priced, well-equipped example of one of Ford's best recent products.
Lightning Blue Metallic is an electric, eye-catching color that suits the Ranger's athletic stance perfectly. The SuperCrew body style gives you a full four-door configuration with enough rear legroom for adult passengers — a meaningful upgrade over the SuperCab setup. The 5-foot bed hits the sweet spot for a mid-size truck buyer: big enough for a full sheet of plywood, small enough to parallel park in Ann Arbor.
Under the hood, the 2019 Ranger is powered exclusively by Ford's 2.3-liter EcoBoost four-cylinder — and in this application it's a revelation. 270 horsepower and 310 lb-ft of torque from a four-cylinder engine gives this Ranger performance that embarrasses similarly-sized trucks from competitors. The 10-speed SelectShift automatic transmission extracts maximum efficiency and performance from the EcoBoost engine, resulting in a driving experience that feels more athletic than utilitarian.
The FX4 Off-Road package (verify on build sheet) is commonly equipped on XLT Rangers and adds locking rear differential, all-terrain tires, underbody protection, and a terrain management system with selectable drive modes. These additions transform the Ranger from a capable truck into a genuinely off-road-ready machine that can handle Michigan's two-track trails and unpaved roads with confidence.
Inside, the SYNC 3 8-inch touchscreen connects to Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, keeping your music, navigation, and calls integrated. SiriusXM satellite radio fills the cab with entertainment coast to coast. Heated front seats are a welcome feature through Michigan's extended cold season. The interior is clean, modern, and thoughtfully designed — a significant step up from the previous-generation Ranger that this model replaced.
